entries.title: Muse, Wings, and a Monkey With a Missing Page
entries.description: A day of agents everywhere: Meta’s shiny new assistant Muse storms the consumer imagination, while the rest of the inbox reminds us the body still runs on vinegar, zucchini, and old books with torn pages.
entries.body:
A day of agents everywhere: Meta’s shiny new assistant Muse storms the consumer imagination, while the rest of the inbox reminds us the body still runs on vinegar, zucchini, and old books with torn pages.

Best links / tech & platforms

• Meta’s Muse as the new metaverse-shaped story to sell — Casey Newton’s take on Muse as Meta’s next “centerpiece,” plus a surprisingly bullish hands-on with the new Meta VR Glasses (lightweight, comfy, puck-based compute). Read: Platformer.

• Personal agents = instant market panic + messy reality — Newcomer surveys the “personal agent race” (Muse vs Instinct), and the practical friction points (CAPTCHAs, bot bans, reservation swarms). Also a fun idea: agents shifting power away from platforms… if the plumbing of commerce can handle an army of bots.

Worth reading (books, ideas, the humanities)

• “The Monkey and the Missing Page: What Are the Humanities For?” — a smart, lived-in essay about what sticks from a humanities education (texture > summaries), with a great mini-horror story about an AI-generated overview confidently claiming “there is no monkey” in Utopia — exactly the point.

Food & places

• Vinegar-braised chicken wings — Alison Roman is in full “it rained once so now I braise” mode: sticky-collagen wings in a bright vinegar-forward sauce with zucchini, raw garlic, and torn herbs. Strong serve for toast, buttered orzo, or rice.

Culture / tonight-only energy

• A sold-out play in East Williamsburg — Downpressors (Jordan Coley): “a crackling political play” about cousins, Jamaican heritage, revolutionary ambitions, and “one extremely annoying (but potentially useful) white friend.” If you’re in Brooklyn and lucky: there’s a waitlist for 8pm / 10pm.

One-liners

• Bots are back, but now they want your bank account and your dinner reservations — and everyone’s scrambling to decide whether to treat them like users, attackers, or interns.
